blocks.text: **Tissue culture** = growing cells, tissues or organs in a sterile nutrient medium in vitro, exploiting **totipotency** (a plant cell's capacity to regenerate a whole plant) and, for animals, cell proliferation. **Plant tissue culture (micropropagation)** is the workhorse: an **explant** (tissue piece) on medium (**MS medium — Murashige-Skoog**) with **plant growth regulators** (auxin-cytokinin balance controlling root/shoot) → **callus** (undifferentiated mass) → **organogenesis/somatic embryogenesis** → plantlets → hardening → field. **Animal cell culture** grows cells (primary or immortalised lines) for research, vaccines and therapeutics.

rows: Mass-clone identical plants from a single explant
Banana, potato, orchids, sugarcane, forestry — disease-free elite planting material (AP's horticulture)
Grow cells in vitro; stem-cell differentiation
Vaccine production, drug testing, regenerative medicine, cultured meat

items: **The agricultural transformation**: tissue culture delivers **disease-free, uniform, mass planting material year-round** — the backbone of high-value horticulture (banana-plantlets, orchids), forestry (clonal eucalyptus-teak), and germplasm conservation (cryo-banks) — a Green-biotech pillar directly serving AP's horticulture leadership.

**The medical-industrial arm**: animal-cell and stem-cell culture underpin vaccine manufacturing (cell-based flu/polio vaccines), toxicity testing (reducing animal use), regenerative medicine (tissue engineering, organoids), and the emerging cultured-meat industry.

**Requirements & limits**: strict asepsis (contamination the enemy), skilled labour, capital (culture labs), and somaclonal variation (unwanted mutations) — the practical constraints; commercial hardening (acclimatisation) is often the failure point.

**AP hook**: tissue-culture banana-and-horticulture (the state's diversification, ADA-036), forestry clones, aqua-hatchery cell techniques, and the pharma-vaccine cell-culture base — tissue culture powering AP's Green and Blue biotech.

sections.heading: The balance and the AP hook

items: **The promise**: cheaper biopharmaceuticals, better livestock, disease research, and organ-supply solutions — transgenic animals could transform medicine and food; India's strength is the base husbandry (world's largest livestock population) that biotech can uplift.

**The concerns (BN-033 applied to animals)**: animal welfare (the ethics of engineering sentient beings), biosafety (transgene escape, ecological risk — AquAdvantage debates), food-safety-acceptance, and the equity/access question — India permits research but is cautious on commercial transgenic animals/food.

**The husbandry-first reality for India**: for most Indian farmers the transformative technologies are the ACCESSIBLE ones — AI, sexed semen, ET, breed improvement, and disease control — not (yet) transgenics; the biotech frontier matters but the mass gains are in conventional-plus-genomic husbandry.

**AP hook**: the strong buffalo-dairy economy (Chittoor-Godavari belts), poultry (AP a major producer), aqua-genetics (the Blue-biotech frontier — selective breeding of shrimp/fish), and AI-ET delivery through veterinary services — husbandry biotech in the state.

blocks.text: **Immunity** = the body's capacity to resist pathogens. Two arms: **innate (non-specific, immediate)** — physical barriers (skin, mucosa), phagocytes (macrophages, neutrophils), NK cells, inflammation, complement, fever; and **adaptive (specific, memory-forming)** — **humoral** (B-cells → antibodies against extracellular pathogens) + **cell-mediated** (T-cells: helper-CD4 coordinate, cytotoxic-CD8 kill infected cells). Key concept: **memory cells** — after first exposure, they enable a faster-stronger response next time (the basis of vaccination). Immunity types: **active** (body makes its own — infection or vaccine, long-lasting) vs **passive** (ready-made antibodies — maternal/antisera, immediate but temporary).

sections.heading: Modern vaccine production — the Hepatitis-B story

items: **The recombinant revolution (the Hepatitis-B exemplar)**: the first-generation Hep-B vaccine was plasma-derived (from carriers' blood — risky, limited); the **recombinant Hep-B vaccine** clones the viral **surface antigen (HBsAg)** gene into **yeast (Saccharomyces)** which mass-produces the pure antigen — safe, scalable, cheap; this is genetic engineering (HB-039) applied to vaccinology — the template for modern subunit vaccines.

**India's vaccine prowess**: ~60% of global vaccine volume; indigenous vaccines (Covaxin, Rotavac, ZyCoV-D-DNA, CERVAVAC-HPV, pneumococcal); the manufacturing base (Serum Institute, Bharat Biotech, Biological E) — the 'vaccine superpower' built on recombinant and cell-culture technology.

**The immunisation delivery**: **Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP)** — one of the world's largest (12+ diseases, ~2.6 crore infants/yr), **Mission Indradhanush** (coverage push), CoWIN (the digital scale-up); the primary-prevention backbone (HB-036).

**AP hook**: the region's vaccine-manufacturing base (Bharat Biotech's Covaxin), UIP delivery through the health system, and Aarogyasri-family-doctor immunisation reach — vaccinology serving the state.

sections.heading: IPR in science & technology — the framework

blocks.text: **Intellectual Property Rights** grant time-limited exclusive rights over creations of the mind, balancing **incentive to innovate** against **public access to knowledge** — the core tension of IP policy. The types: **patents** (inventions — novel, non-obvious, useful; 20-year term), **copyright** (creative-literary works, software), **trademarks** (brand identity), **designs** (aesthetic form), **geographical indications (GI)** (origin-linked products — hugely relevant for India), **trade secrets, plant-variety protection**, and **traditional-knowledge** protection (the TKDL innovation).

rows: **Patents Act 1970 (TRIPS-amended 2005)**; **Section 3(d)** — bars evergreening (the **Novartis-Glivec case, 2013** — India's public-health-protecting jurisprudence); **compulsory licensing (Sec 84 — Bayer Nexavar, 2012)** for access

**GI Act 1999**; India has 600+ GIs — **Tirupati laddu, Banginapalle mango, Guntur Sannam chilli, Bandar laddu, Kondapalli/Etikoppaka toys, Machilipatnam Kalamkari, Dharmavaram/Venkatagiri/Uppada sarees, Araku coffee** (the AP GI treasure)
**TKDL (Traditional Knowledge Digital Library, 2001)** — prior-art database that defeated the **neem and turmeric** patents (biopiracy wins)
**National IPR Policy 2016** ('Creative India, Innovative India'), CGPDTM (patent office), the push to lift India's low patent-filing (rising fast — resident filings crossed non-resident 2022)
**PPV&FR Act 2001** — unique dual protection of breeders' AND farmers' rights (India's sui-generis model)

items: **The access-vs-incentive balance**: strong IP rewards R&D but can price out the poor (medicines the sharpest case); India's stance — **TRIPS-compliant but public-health-protective** (Sec 3(d), compulsory licensing, the 'pharmacy of the world' generics) — a globally-watched model balancing the two; the TRIPS-waiver advocacy (Covid vaccines) extended it.

**India's own innovation-IP gap**: historically low patent-filing (services-not-products economy), university-tech-transfer weakness, and the challenge of moving from IP-user to IP-creator — ANRF, patent-office reform and startup-IP support the answers; resident patent filings now rising sharply.

**GI as development tool**: India's GI wealth (especially AP's) protects artisan-farmer livelihoods, commands price premiums, and prevents misappropriation — GI is IP working for the traditional economy; the challenge is post-registration marketing and enforcement.

**AP hook**: the state's GI treasure (Banginapalle mango, Guntur chilli, Kondapalli-Etikoppaka toys, Kalamkari, Araku coffee, the sarees), pharma-generics manufacturing (the Sec 3(d) beneficiary), and traditional-knowledge (Eastern-Ghats ethnobotany) — IP working across AP's economy.

sections.heading: Promotion of science — India and AP

blocks.text: Promoting science means building the **pipeline (talent), the plumbing (funding-institutions), the culture (scientific temper), and the application (innovation-commercialisation)**. India's promotion architecture: **funding** (DST, DBT, CSIR, **ANRF 2023 ₹50,000 cr**), **talent** (INSPIRE scholarships, KVPY-legacy, Olympiads, PMRF fellowships), **culture** (National Science Day, science communication — Vigyan Prasar, science cities-museums), **innovation** (Atal Innovation Mission, tinkering labs, Startup India, incubators), and **missions** (Quantum, AI, Semicon, Deep Ocean). The constitutional mandate: **Article 51A(h)** — the citizen's duty to develop **scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform** (Nehru's phrase, constitutionalised).

rows: IISc, IITs, IISERs, national labs, ANRF
**IIT/IISER Tirupati, Central University AP, NARL Gadanki, Sriharikota**; state S&T council (APCOST)

items: **The binding constraints**: low R&D spend (0.65% GDP — the perennial), private-R&D under-share, brain-drain-to-circulation, weak university-industry-lab linkage, research-integrity issues, and gender-regional gaps in science — promotion means attacking each; **ANRF (2023)** is the flagship attempt to coordinate funding and pull private R&D.

**Scientific temper as culture**: promotion isn't only labs and money — it's a **society that thinks scientifically** (evidence over superstition, inquiry over dogma); Article 51A(h)'s mandate matters against pseudoscience and for evidence-based policy — a values point examiners reward.

**The AP-specific promotion story**: post-bifurcation rebuild (Hyderabad's labs gone — STNB-004), leaning on Sriharikota, Gadanki-NARL, Tirupati's institutes, APCOST, aqua-marine and natural-farming science, and the innovation-ecosystem ambitions (Vizag as a science-tech hub) — an honest state-promotion assessment.

**The synthesis**: raise R&D, widen participation, build scientific temper, and connect lab-to-market — for India and, from a rebuilding base, for AP; science promotion is human-capital investment with the longest, highest returns. This completes Paper-V at 46/46.
